knowledge_point: Solving Cubic Equations by Manipulating the Equation and Then Grouping
worked_solution:
First, we subtract $8{y}^{2}$ and $3y$ from both sides to make the right side $0.$ To prepare for factoring by grouping, we make sure to write the resulting cubic in standard form.

$$
6{y}^{3}-8{y}^{2}-3y+4=0
$$

Next, we factor by grouping. Notice that when grouping the smaller terms, we factor out the negative sign.

$$
\begin{aligned}6{y}^{3}-8{y}^{2}-3y+4 & = \\ (6{y}^{3}-8{y}^{2})-(3y-4) & = \\ 2{y}^{2}(3y-4)-(3y-4) & = \\ (3y-4)\cdot 2{y}^{2}-(3y-4)\cdot 1 & = \\ (3y-4)(2{y}^{2}-1) & .\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we set each factor equal to $0$ and solve.

- Setting the factor $(3y-4)$ equal to $0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}3y-4 & =0 \\ 3y & =4 \\ y & =\frac{4}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

- Setting the factor $(2{y}^{2}-1)$ equal to $0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2{y}^{2}-1 & =0 \\ 2{y}^{2} & =1 \\ {y}^{2} & =\frac{1}{2} \\ y & =\pm \sqrt{\frac{1}{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solutions are $y=\frac{4}{3},\,\pm \sqrt{\frac{1}{2}}.$
